subject: Why are factor scores correlated, even though I modeled the latent variables as independent?

messages.author: ccdd463843cf5f95
messages.subject: Why are factor scores correlated, even though I modeled the latent variables as independent?
parts:
Hi all,

I use this model to describe my data:

model <- 'LV1 =~ 1 * indicator1 +
                            1 * indicator2 +
                            1 * indicator3 +
                            1 * indicator4
                LV2 =~ 1 * indicator1 +
                            2 * indicator2 +
                            3 * indicator3 +
                            4 * indicator4
                LV1 ~~ 0 * LV2'

Modelfit is very good with CS(4) = 6.01, p = .19. I always assumed that the command LV1 ~~ 0 * LV2 sets the covariance between the latent variables to zero, and obviously it does, giving me a covariance estimate of LV1 ~~ LV2 = 0.000. However, if I use

factorscoresLV1 <- predict[, 1]
factorscoresLV2 <- predict[, 2]
corr.test(data.frame(factorscoresLV1, factorscoresLV2)

the output says the correlation is –.08 (n. s.). Can anybody clarify, why the factor scores are correlated, even though I fixed the covariance between the latent variables to zero?

Thanks in advance,
Philipp

messages.author: bfa43814f6ba1969
messages.subject: Re: Why are factor scores correlated, even though I modeled the latent variables as independent?
parts:
Hi

Lavaan calculate regression factor scores, which maximize the expected correlation between the factor scores and the true factor values. The regression factor scores are not correlation preserving. Here is a good article on various different ways for calculating factor scores:

Grice, J. W. (2001). Computing and evaluating factor scores. Psychological Methods, 6(4), 430.

Do you need correlation preserving factor scores or are you just interested in learning more about factor scores?

Mikko

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Why are factor scores correlated, even though I modeled the latent variables as independent?
parts:
Philipp,
It is not clear what you mean by the factor scores used for the SEM.  I do not know which estimation method you used, but the parameters in the SEM are estimated without any need for estimated factor scores.  Independence between two latent variables is a property implied jointly by several different features of your model specification rather than being a single feature (parameter) of the model specification.  (We might go a step further to say that non-covariance is so implied and this in turn implies independence when combined with an assumption of linearity.)  In your example, some of these features are explicit (zero covariance) and some implicit (zero direct or indirect effects).  Because you specified a model with orthogonal latent variables, the parameter estimation and fit assessment reflect that implication of the model.  However, no factor scores were used to generate the estimates, statistics or indices included in the output.  The estimation chapter of any good SEM text will provide more details. 

Keith

Keith A. Markus
John Jay College of Criminal Justice, CUNY
http://jjcweb.jjay.cuny.edu/kmarkus
Frontiers of Test Validity Theory: Measurement, Causation and Meaning.
http://www.routledge.com/books/details/9781841692203/
